newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Supreme Court judge shot dead in ETA attack.
newsitem.headline: Spain Supreme Court judge shot dead in ETA attack.

text.p: A Spanish Supreme Court judge was shot dead on Monday and a serviceman killed by a car bomb in what authorities believe were attacks by the Basque separatist group ETA.
Judge Rafael Martinez, 68, was shot in the head outside his home in central Madrid. He died on the way to hospital, police said.
"This is the voice of ETA," said Deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez Cascos.
"We will not bend in the face of this terror, violence and death," he added. The government would not enter talks with the guerrilla group.
Police said they had found a weapon commonly used by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) close to the scene of the crime.
The attack came just hours after a car bomb exploded in the southern city of Granada killing one man and injuring seven, another action the government blamed on ETA.
Madrid police said they feared the getaway vehicle used by the judge's attacker and so far not found would be set to explode -- a common method used by ETA to destroy evidence.
Spain's High Court said Monday's attack was likely to have been a reprisal for the imprisonment of a number of leaders of ETA's political wing, Herri Batasuna (HB).
The Supreme Court sent five HB leaders to prison last week after they failed to appear in court to answer charges that they promoted violence.
"This is a brutal attempt to intimidate the courts so the judges will not carry out their duties," said Clemente Auger, president of the High Court.
"Despite the grief, our fellow judges will continue to fulfil their jurisdiction, without exercising any revenge or intimidation."
Police said the judge had been shot in his doorway just after 2.30 p.m. (1330 GMT).
"A bullet...passed through the nape of his neck and out the forehead...he did not respond to our resuscitation efforts," emergency services said.
ETA killed another judge almost exactly a year ago, shooting ex-constitutional court judge Francisco Tomas y Valiente in his office in Madrid.
Martinez's is the fourth death this year attributed to the guerrilla group. ETA shot dead an army officer in Madrid and a bicycle vendor in San Sebastian.
ETA has killed some 800 people in its 29-year drive for an independent Basque state.
